stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is behind on continuing education for the current calendar year. She attends an intensive live conference held on a single day in December and the authorized provider issues her a statement of credit for 12 contact hours earned that day. She wants to apply all 12 to that calendar year. How many of those contact hours may she apply?

choices.text: The full 12, because the daily restriction applies to home study rather than live programs.
The full 12, because live conference programming carries no daily restriction.
Ten, because a registrant may not exceed ten contact hours in a calendar day.
None, because contact hours earned in December are credited to the following cycle.
Eight, because a registrant may not earn more than eight contact hours in a calendar day.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 4.03(7) provides that a registrant may not earn more than eight contact hours of continuing education in a calendar day. The provision is written without reference to delivery format, so it binds a live conference as it would home study, and it caps the day rather than the year. Eight of the 12 hours issued for that single day may therefore be applied.

choice_analysis.A: 247 CMR 4.03(7) is silent as to format; the home-study limit is the separate 15-hour annual cap in 247 CMR 4.03(4)(b).
choice_analysis.B: The daily cap is not disapplied for live programming.
choice_analysis.C: The figure in 247 CMR 4.03(7) is eight contact hours, not ten.
choice_analysis.D: No provision defers December hours to the following cycle; hours are attributed to the calendar year in which they are earned.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the daily cap is eight contact hours.

related_facts: Contact hours may not be carried over from one calendar year to another under 247 CMR 4.03(5).
explanation.mpje_trap: The annual arithmetic is a distraction: a single day cannot yield more than eight contact hours however long the programme runs or however it is delivered.

reasoning_steps: Recognise that the constraint at issue is a per-calendar-day cap rather than an annual total
Note that 247 CMR 4.03(7) does not distinguish delivery format
Apply the eight-hour figure to the single day of attendance
